newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares little changed in trendless trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares little changed in trendless trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged on Tuesday amid mild profit-taking and traders said the positive trend is expected to continue in the short term.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.03 percent, or 0.09 points, to 309.79 on an all-share turnover of 221 million shekels against 216 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.21 percent lower at 316.68.

"The market made a very nice move recently and the Maof index is getting closer to 320, which is seen by technical analysts as a resistance line," said Ronen Kaufman at Nesuah Trading and Investments.
"The market is gaining strength to continue its rise. It was trying to consolidate today with little success," he said.

"Today we saw some profit-taking but the market was showing strength. In the near term the market is expected to continue rising but in the long run we will see a correction," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.

Kaufman said that the market will continue to rise in the near future. "The positive trend is supported by falling bond yields, mutual funds' positive returns, new foreign money, a rise in world markets and good earning reports," he said.

Dead Sea Works surged 4.25 percent to 1,222 agorot (Israeli cents). The company reported on Tuesday that second quarter earnings per share rose to 15 agorot from 11 agorot at the same period last year.
Lehman Brothers started coverage of Dead Sea on Tuesday rating it "neutral". The investment bank said the company was fully valued at 21.3 expected earnings for 1997.
Elbit Systems rose 3.25 percent to 5,155 agorot. Elbit reported on Monday that earnings per share in the second quarter rose to $0.43 from $0.36 a share a year earlier.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 0.75 percent to 20,651 agorot on volume of 19.9 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which gained 0.75 percent to 588 agorot on turnover of 7.7 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which rose 2.0 percent to 427 agorot on volume of 5.3 million shekels.
